cases.settings: Design the Settings screen for Waymark, a map app for community walking groups. Deliver two static frames in one self-contained HTML: desktop light 720 × 640 with a 208 px left rail, and phone dark 390 × 844. The desktop is open at Account; the phone at Devices. Sections are General, Notifications, Account, Devices, Organizations, Apps, API keys, in Preferences and Developer groups. Account has Name, Username, Email, Password, Save in the header, Sign out and Delete account at the foot. Devices shows this device and two other signed-in devices with last-active information, and Sign out of other devices at the foot. Rows open detail cards and have a chevron, no trailing action buttons. Back and Close are outlined; titles left-aligned. Section groups use labels and space, no horizontal dividers. Use one font family, light and dark from shared semantic tokens, no literal component colours. Phone actions take a full line. English text. No extra sections or sign-in notices. All content must fit the specified frames with no scrolling, clipping or overlap. Data is fictional. This is a static visual design test: no functional flows required. Choose the aesthetic yourself. Include concise decisions and inspect the final rendered frames.
cases.operations: Design a static dispatch board for Tidal, a service that coordinates repairs of public drinking fountains. One desktop frame, 1440 × 900, all content visible without scrolling. Audience: a dispatcher checking the next two hours. Show today's date, three meaningful summary figures (open jobs, urgent jobs, crews available), a work queue of eight jobs with site, fault, priority, assigned crew and promised arrival; highlight one selected urgent job. Show its detailed panel with reported issue, last update, a small 3-step service history and an Assign crew primary action. Also show three crews and availability. English, fictional but coherent data. The user must distinguish urgent work from unassigned work and see what to do next. No charts or map are required. No existing brand colours or fonts: choose a specific appropriate visual direction. Do not add unrelated features. Deliver one self-contained static HTML and a 1440 × 900 PNG, with concise decisions. No interaction implementation is required; inspect the final render.
cases.poster: Design an event poster as one static HTML frame, exactly 900 × 1200, for NIGHT SIGNALS: an evening programme of live electronic music and projected light at a former municipal water tower. Fictional event: Saturday 21 November 2026, doors 19:00, performances 20:00–23:30, Tower Hall, 14 Canal Road. Acts: Mara Vale (live modular set), Ivo & Nera (tape loops), Field Array (light installation). Tickets €18 advance / €24 door. Include the title, location, date/time, lineup and ticket information, plus one short line that describes the experience. Design should feel specific to sound, light and the vertical industrial space; it must work as a poster viewed from a distance and reward close reading. Choose typography, palette and composition freely. Use typography, CSS or original geometric SVG; no photos or external image generation. No application controls, cards, navigation or drawn browser chrome. English. All content fits, no scrolling or clipping. Deliver self-contained HTML, a 900 × 1200 PNG and concise decisions. Inspect the final render.
cases.document: Design a one-page annual impact brief for the fictional Canal Library, a neighbourhood lending library. It is a document for members to read closely, not a marketing landing page or an application. Deliver one static self-contained HTML page and PNG, exactly 900 × 1200, with all content visible and no scrolling. Use only one font family, a white background, dark text and at most one restrained accent of your choice. No horizontal rules anywhere, no decorative numbering, no large hero headline, no buttons or navigation. Title: Canal Library — 2026 in review. Content: 1,240 active members, 18,460 loans, 68 public sessions; compare with 2025 values 1,080, 16,200 and 54 respectively. Include a readable table of three programme strands: Reading circles (28 sessions, 340 visits), Repair afternoons (16 sessions, 210 visits), Young storytellers (24 sessions, 420 visits). Explain that visits can include repeat attendance. Include a short paragraph about why Sunday opening was introduced, one clearly marked member quotation (fictional), and a compact 2027 plan: retain Sunday opening, add two accessible reading stations, pilot one monthly evening session. English text; all figures and quote are fictional and should be marked discreetly. Establish a calm, legible hierarchy for close reading, with exact labels and coherent data. No photos or image generation. Choose composition and type treatment independently. Include concise decisions and inspect the final render.
